value.body: Each state's power sector is run by state-owned companies. After the Electricity Act, 2003, most former State Electricity Boards were split into separate generation, transmission and distribution companies. They recruit engineering graduates as Assistant Engineers to run power plants, substations, transmission lines and local distribution networks.

items.label: Entry post
items.note: Junior Engineer posts are for diploma holders

items.label: Main discipline
items.note: Civil, mechanical, electronics and others also recruited

items.label: State-sector coal-based capacity
items.note: About a third of India's coal-based capacity

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A B.E./B.Tech in the discipline named in the notification. Utilities recruit through their own written exams, through the state Public Service Commission, or on GATE scores in some states. Age limits, domicile and language requirements follow the state's rules.

value.title: At a glance
items: Each utility recruits on its own timetable; gaps between notifications are common.
Work includes field duty, breakdown response and shift work at plants and substations.
Knowledge of the state language and domicile rules often apply.
Central power PSUs recruit separately, mostly through GATE.

value.title: Installed generating capacity by owner
value.note: Generation capacity only, all sources including renewables; it does not show transmission or distribution, where state companies also operate.
